claims.value: Bodart: side A (French) 13,000 infantry and 3,000 cavalry, total 16,000; side B (Portuguese) 23,000, three quarters irregulars.
claims.rationale: Claim-relevant rendering of the contextual quote/table. Bodart’s rounded-up available-for-engagement convention is shared, not an opening muster. Source-specific component/time distinctions remain. English rendering (ours): "Side A: 13,000 infantry and 3,000 cavalry, total 16,000. Side B: 23,000, three quarters irregulars."

claims.rationale: Approach population; does not replace Bodart’s battle total. English rendering (ours): "He entered with 21,000 men, Silveira withdrawing toward Villa Pouca."

claims.value: Le Noble estimates side B at 40,000 with artillery seen on the 17 March approach.
claims.rationale: French opponent estimate on the approach, not an original Portuguese return or a matched 20 March count. English rendering (ours): "There the enemy was recognized as forty thousand men with cannon."

claims.rationale: Two mediated accounts, not two inspected Portuguese command orders. English rendering (ours): "After Freyre’s death Eben took chief command; his second, Baron Ebben, had to defend Carballo with collected troops."

claims.value: Le Noble describes the approach beyond the Cavado bridge as too narrow for artillery, rock on one side and a precipice on the other.
claims.rationale: Approach terrain, not a claim that all guns were absent from the battle. English rendering (ours): "Beyond the Cavado bridge the path was too narrow for artillery, rock on the left and a precipice on the right."
